data.body:
RCA (complete; investigation only)

OBSERVATION
The gate scratch guard has four marker quadrants. The intended fail-loud case is declaration present + proof absent; the current no-declaration quadrant admits the gate. Terraform declares and attaches `aws_ebs_volume.gate_scratch` at `var.gate_scratch_mount`, but `infra/terraform/user_data.sh` is the only committed boot path that writes both `/var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required` and `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted`. A volume attached after first boot can therefore exist in AWS and monitoring while the host remains in the no-declaration quadrant forever.

HYPOTHESIS
`src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py:scratch_unavailable_detail` keys admission only off the root-side marker `_SCRATCH_REQUIRED_MARKER`; if that file is absent, it returns `None` before checking the proof marker. Because the declaration writer is first-boot `infra/terraform/user_data.sh`, not Terraform state or a recurring reconciler, post-launch attachment cannot make the fail-loud branch reachable.

CONFIRMATION
Confirmed with an isolated session scratch host (no repo or production writes): with `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` pointed at a simulated `/var/gate-scratch` path and no declaration marker, `scratch_unavailable_detail()` returned `None` and `gate_admission(...)` admitted the gate. Adding only `.gate-scratch-required` immediately changed the same path to a `GateScratchUnavailableError`. This would have been disproven if a declared Terraform/attached-volume signal independent of the root-side marker were consulted before returning `None`.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION
Preserve opt-in behavior for laptops/CI, but derive “this host should have dedicated scratch” from a source that survives post-boot attachment: e.g. host config/manifest maintained by provisioning plus repair tooling, or Terraform-rendered expected mount data consumed by a periodic reconciler. Also decide whether to data-drive the repeated expected mount set in user_data, check-mounts, and observability.
